text: No. The Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, and my earlier statement was wrong. At about 384,000 km, no individual human structure is resolvable; even continents show only as large-scale color and cloud patterns. The wall is also long but only about 5-9 m wide, and it is similar in color to its surroundings. Astronauts report that it is hard to pick out even from low Earth orbit (~400 km) without magnification and ideal conditions, and Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei said he couldn't see it on his 2003 flight.
